summary: Australia's PBAC has no explicit threshold but empirically recommends drugs much more readily below ~AUD 30,000/QALY and rarely above ~AUD 70,000-75,000/QALY, with an effective threshold near AUD 28,000-50,000/QALY (about USD 18,500-33,000 in 2024).
source_citation: Wang et al., Pharmaceutical Medicine (2015), https://link.springer.com/article/10.1007/s40290-014-0063-5; Karnon, ISPOR 2022, https://www.ispor.org/docs/default-source/asia2022/ispor-2022-karnon.pdf . Source range AUD 28,000-50,000/QALY (analyses ~2014-2018; rule-of-thumb AUD 50,000, empirical effective ~AUD 28,000); 2024 USD at AUD/USD 0.6598 gives ~USD 18,500-33,000; midpoint ~USD 25,750.

summary: Canada's CADTH consistently applies a willingness-to-pay benchmark of CAD 50,000 per QALY (about USD 36,500 in 2024) as a de facto cost-effectiveness threshold, though it publishes no formal value.
source_citation: Skedgel et al., "CADTH's $50,000 Cost-Effectiveness Threshold: Fact or Fiction," Value in Health (2016), https://www.valueinhealthjournal.com/article/S1098-3015(16)32187-8/fulltext; oncology-drug WTP review, PubMed 38567953, https://pubmed.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/38567953/ . Source value CAD 50,000/QALY (constant 2021-2022 CADTH reviews), 2024 USD at USD/CAD 1.3702; described as an arbitrary, un-inflation-adjusted legacy figure.

summary: A 2020-2021 Chinese contingent-valuation survey of 2,008 respondents found a mean willingness-to-pay of RMB 113,120 per QALY (USD 16,884, ~1.75x GDP per capita), with life extension (RMB 177,761) valued about 2.25x quality-of-life improvement (RMB 78,907).
source_citation: Yang et al., Applied Health Economics and Health Policy (2022), https://link.springer.com/article/10.1007/s40258-022-00750-z; PMC9358064, https://pmc.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/articles/PMC9358064/ . Source mean RMB 113,120/QALY ~ USD 16,884 (2020-2021); QoL RMB 78,907 (USD 11,777, 1.22x GDP) vs life-extension RMB 177,761 (USD 26,531, 2.76x GDP), life-ext ~2.25x QoL; ~USD 17,500-18,000 in 2024; midpoint ~USD 17,750.

summary: The EuroVaQ survey of 17,657 respondents across 9 European countries elicited a pooled all-countries willingness-to-pay of EUR 14,430-26,965 per QALY (about USD 19,000-35,500 in 2024), with imminent-death life extension (~EUR 29,000) valued above coma avoidance (~EUR 19,000) and quality-of-life-only gains (~EUR 11,000).
jurisdiction: Europe (9 countries: UK, Netherlands, France, Spain, Norway, Sweden, Denmark, Hungary, Poland)
source_citation: Donaldson/Robinson et al. (EuroVaQ), Social Science & Medicine (2013), https://www.sciencedirect.com/science/article/abs/pii/S0277953613002876; CORDIS project, https://cordis.europa.eu/project/id/44172 . Source pooled range EUR 14,430-26,965/QALY (chained TTO/SG + WTP, survey ~2010 PPP EUR); ~USD 19,000-35,500 in 2024 (rough); midpoint ~USD 27,250. Life-extension > coma-avoidance > QoL-only gradient noted.

summary: A Japanese internet contingent-valuation survey (~1,114 respondents aged 20-59) produced a nonparametric estimate of JPY 5.0 million per QALY (about USD 41,000 at the survey-era rate, ~USD 34,000 in 2024), which became the reference anchor in Japan's HTA system.
source_citation: Shiroiwa et al., Health Economics (2010), international WTP-per-QALY survey, https://ideas.repec.org/a/wly/hlthec/v19y2010i4p422-437.html; Japan HTA overview, Value in Health (2019), https://www.valueinhealthjournal.com/article/S1098-3015(19)35170-8/fulltext . Source JPY 5.0M/QALY (Turnbull estimate, survey ~2008-2009) = USD 41,000 at earlier stronger-yen rate; at ~150 JPY/USD (2024) materially lower, ~USD 33,000-35,000; midpoint ~USD 34,000. Became Japan HTA reference anchor.

summary: The Netherlands' Zorginstituut applies severity-differentiated thresholds via proportional shortfall of EUR 20,000, 50,000, and 80,000 per QALY (least to most severe; about USD 21,600, 54,000, and 86,500 in 2024), with the EUR 80,000 ceiling reserved for the most severe conditions.
label_raw: ZIN tiered ceiling EUR 20k/50k/80k per QALY (budget threshold, severity-varied)
source_citation: Reckers-Droog et al., Value in Health (2021) on severity-varied WTP, https://www.valueinhealthjournal.com/article/S1098-3015(21)01690-9/fulltext; van Baal et al., Health Economics (2019), https://onlinelibrary.wiley.com/doi/full/10.1002/hec.3831 . Source values EUR 20,000/50,000/80,000 per QALY (framework ~2015 onward); 2024 USD at EUR/USD ~1.08 gives ~USD 21,600/54,000/86,500; money_value_usd2024 records the most-severe EUR 80,000 tier.

summary: A 2015 South Korean contingent-valuation study (507 interviews) found willingness-to-pay rising from KRW 15M per QALY (non-cure) through KRW 22M (5-year) and 27M (10-year prolongation) to KRW 35M for lifetime cure (about 2.3x the non-cure value; roughly USD 11,000-26,000 in 2024).
source_citation: Lim et al., Medicine (2018), https://pmc.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/articles/PMC6160178/ . Source scenario WTP/QALY: non-cure KRW 15M, 5-yr KRW 22M, 10-yr KRW 27M, lifetime cure KRW 35M (2.3x non-cure), higher for severe than mild (2015 KRW); ~USD 11,000 (non-cure) to ~USD 25,700 (cure) at ~1,360 KRW/USD, ~USD 11,000-26,000 in 2024; midpoint ~USD 18,500.

summary: A 2008 Thai TTO-based contingent-valuation study (1,191 respondents) found treatment willingness-to-pay of 59,000-285,000 THB per QALY (about USD 2,500-13,000 in 2024) varying strongly by condition (paralysis 59k-101k, blindness 185k-285k) and exceeding prevention values, the empirical counterpart to HITAP's budget ceiling.
source_citation: Nimdet/Thavorncharoensap et al., "Estimating the WTP for a QALY in Thailand," PMC3548562, https://pmc.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/articles/PMC3548562/ . Source treatment 59,000-285,000 THB/QALY, prevention 26,000-137,000 THB (2008; ~USD 3,578-17,283 PPP; ~0.4-2x 2008 GDP/capita); context-dependent (blindness 185k-285k, paralysis 59k-101k); ~USD 2,500-13,000 in 2024 (rough); midpoint ~USD 7,750.

summary: Thailand's HITAP sets an explicit cost-effectiveness ceiling of 160,000 THB per QALY (raised from 100,000 in 2008 to 120,000 in 2010 to 160,000 in 2013, roughly 1.0-1.3x GDP per capita; about USD 4,600 in 2024).
source_citation: OHE "Around the World in HTAs: Thailand," https://www.ohe.org/insights/around-the-world-in-htas-thailand/; Teerawattananon, ISPOR AP 2018, https://www.ispor.org/docs/default-source/conference-ap-2018/teerawattananon-ispor_panel-ce_threshold-v3.pdf . Source value 160,000 THB/QALY set 2013 (~1.0-1.3x GDP/capita); ~USD 4,500-4,700 in 2024 USD; exact 2024-USD uncertain due to baht inflation/FX.

summary: A meta-regression of 39 willingness-to-pay studies (511 observations) estimates a pooled mean of USD 52,619 per QALY in 2018 dollars (about USD 65,000 in 2024 after ~24% CPI adjustment), anchored to US 2018 dollars.
label_raw: US pooled empirical mean USD 52,619/QALY (2018 USD)
source_citation: Nimdet/related meta-regression, EJHE (2022), https://link.springer.com/article/10.1007/s10198-021-01364-3; PubMed 34417905, https://pubmed.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/34417905/ . Source value USD 52,619/QALY (95% CI 49,953-55,286), 2018 USD; ~USD 65,000 in 2024 after ~24% cumulative US CPI 2018->2024; pooled cross-country anchored to US 2018 dollars.
